discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat-band correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: strongly correlated electrons and moire materials
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (2011) predicted that at a 'magic' twist angle the Dirac bands of bilayer graphene become almost flat, so that interactions should dominate kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group confirmed this experimentally, finding correlated insulating states and superconductivity whose phase diagram strikingly resembles the cuprates. They did this in a single, gate-tunable, chemically clean device. This work created the field of moiré quantum matter. It gives us a controllable platform where strong correlation, band topology, nematicity, orbital magnetism and unconventional pairing can be studied side by side, and it has led to fractional Chern insulators and the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect. The approach is a minimal, physically transparent idea followed by decisive experiments, and it has changed how the community frames the problem of strongly correlated electrons. Its influence has grown steadily for more than seven years.
